# Introduction

This report examines whether Agreeableness predicts responses to the personality item "Get angry easily" using ordinal logistic regression. The analysis uses the Big Five Inventory (BFI) dataset.

# Data Preparation

## Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(psych)
library(ordinal)
library(readxl)
library(ggeffects)
library(broom)
library(gt)

```

## Import the dataset

```{r}
data <- read_excel("./bfi.xlsx")

data[, 2:26] <- lapply(data[, 2:26], as.integer)
```

## Convert personality item responses to numeric values

```{r}
bfi <- bfi |>
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("...1"))

data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(A1:O5, as.numeric))

str(data)
```

# Score the Big Five personality dimensions

```{r}
keys <- list(
  Agreeableness = c("-A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5"),
  Conscientiousness = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "-C4", "-C5"),
  Extraversion = c("-E1", "-E2", "E3", "E4", "E5"),
  Neuroticism = c("N1", "N2", "N3", "N4", "N5"),
  Openness = c("O1", "-O2", "O3", "O4", "-O5")
)

scores <- scoreItems(
  keys,
  data,
  totals = FALSE,
  min = 1,
  max = 6
)

# Inspect the scoring results
head(scores$scores)
```
